edge_board.description:
**Recent labor market softening has tilted trader consensus toward no change at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, outweighing lingering inflation pressures.** 

July nonfarm payrolls contracted by 23,000—the first outright decline in years—with downward revisions to prior months, while the unemployment rate eased to 4.1%. This cooling, alongside stable but not overheating growth, has reduced the perceived urgency for immediate tightening. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, with headline PCE near 3.7% in June and CPI at 3.4% year-over-year in July, though some moderation appeared in recent prints amid easing energy pressures from earlier Middle East supply disruptions. 

The July FOMC hold (9-3 vote, with three dissents favoring a 25 bp hike) underscored internal divisions, but incoming data since then have lowered market-implied odds of a September increase. Traders view the decision as data-dependent, with August employment and inflation releases due before the meeting serving as key catalysts. A stronger-than-expected inflation rebound or sharp labor rebound could revive hike pricing, while further softening would reinforce expectations for patience.
edge_board.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the September 2026 meeting?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

edge_board.description: **Recent economic data and Fed communications have positioned a September hold as the consensus outcome among traders.** Persistent but not sharply accelerating inflation—July PCE at 3.7% headline and 3.3% core—has kept tightening in play, yet softer July employment figures and mixed August readings have tempered the case for immediate action. The FOMC’s July decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75% (with three dissents favoring a 25 bp hike) and subsequent minutes underscored a data-dependent approach, while Chair Warsh’s hawkish emphasis on returning inflation to target has sustained roughly 30% odds of a modest increase. Cooling labor-market momentum and the political calendar ahead of November midterms have raised the bar for a move, favoring patience unless incoming inflation or jobs data reaccelerate. Low probabilities attached to cuts reflect inflation remaining well above the 2% goal.

edge_board.description: United Russia maintains a commanding position in trader consensus for securing the largest share of State Duma seats in the September 18–20, 2026, election due to its status as the dominant incumbent party, extensive administrative resources, and advantages in the mixed electoral system combining party-list proportional representation with single-member districts. Recent state-affiliated polls from FOM and WCIOM project the party winning a stable majority of seats despite vote shares in the low-to-mid 30s, reinforced by candidate approvals at its June congress, inclusion of military veterans, and favorable ballot positioning in regional contests. New People has registered gains in some surveys, narrowing the gap among smaller parties, while disqualifications such as the Supreme Court’s August removal of Yabloko from the federal list have further consolidated the field. These dynamics, alongside historical patterns of ruling-party seat advantages, underpin current implied probabilities.
edge_board.question: Will United Russia (ER) gain the most seats in the next Russian parliamentary election?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections are to be scheduled to be held in Russia in September 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party that gains the greatest number of seats in the next Russian State Duma election, compared to before the election.

If the results are not known definitively by September 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats gained, this market will resolve in favor of the party that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats gained by the named party in the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results reported by Russian government sources such as the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation.

edge_board.question: Fed rate hike in 2026?
edge_board.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between January 1, 2026 and the Fed's December 2026 meeting, currently scheduled for December 8-9, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market may not resolve to "No" until the Fed has released its rate change decision following its December meeting.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

edge_board.description: Carlos Alcaraz leads the 2026 US Open winner market at 33.5% implied probability after Jannik Sinner’s pre-tournament knee withdrawal and Alcaraz’s own straight-sets first-round win on return from a four-month wrist injury. Alexander Zverev sits at 23.8% as the top seed and recent French Open champion with strong hard-court results, while the open draw has lifted American contenders Ben Shelton (8.1%) and Taylor Fritz (7.4%) along with emerging talents like Rafael Jodar. Novak Djokovic’s first-round exit further redistributed equity among the field, with traders pricing in Alcaraz’s experience on Laykold courts and the competitive but thinned top half of the bracket. Recent form, injury recoveries, and bracket positioning continue to shape these probabilities heading into the early rounds.
edge_board.question: Will Alexander Zverev win the 2026 Men's US Open?

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
